title: Epic: Post-blackout recovery reliability
description:
## Background
power_failure_resumer discovers crash-clustered Codex/Claude sessions and reopens them in Ghostty. Idea-wizard + plan-space refinement (2026-08-03) produced this epic. Concurrent agent **Fable** is also auditing/fixing live code (`pfr-arh` in_progress) — implementers must re-read files before editing and never revert peer work.

## Goals
- One-command trustworthy post-blackout recovery
- Plan/decide/open separation with confidence scoring
- Human-readable session identity for picks
- Doctor + notify-only post-boot (never surprise auto-open)
- Verify opens; skip already-running (matcher shipped)
- Comprehensive unit + e2e tests with NDJSON logs

## Non-Goals
- Full multi-host NTM/SSH swarm resume
- Depending on casr binary (optional enrichment only)
- Guaranteeing model-side resume semantics

## Critical path (ready → blocked)
1. `pfr-test-scaffold-jfl` + `pfr-discover-cli-roots-2k6` (fixture isolation)
2. `pfr-plan-schema-l81` → `pfr-plan-cli-7pj` → plan tests + e2e dry
3. `pfr-extract-titles-akt` → list UX + title tests
4. `pfr-open-verify-3dd` → verify tests (skip-running already CLOSED)
5. `pfr-doctor-cmd-on2` → doctor tests → autoboot notify (needs plan + config)

## Invariants learned (do not regress)
- Cluster **before** filtering already-running
- Tight `resume <uuid>` process matching
- Ghostty: always dedicated tab; no double Cmd+T after partial native open
- Codex id from filename / session_meta.payload.id; Claude titles custom>ai>user
- Confidence HIGH only for pre_boot, never density-only

## Success
User reboots after power loss, runs `pfr` (or sees notify), reviews a HIGH-confidence plan with titles, opens the right tabs, gets a verification report, can re-run safely via `--last-plan`.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Plan-space revision pass: restored empty plan-cli body; added 6 test beads (titles, verify, doctor, config-batch, open-scripts, audit); fixed test graph so live Ghostty is opt-in; confidence NEVER high for density-only; skip-running marked done inside verify feature; casr is optional enrich only.

title: Plan files + crash confidence scoring
description:
## What
Introduce a durable **recovery plan** artifact and a crash **confidence score**, so discovery and open are separable and re-runnable.

## Why
Under stress after a blackout, users need to inspect, edit, and re-open the same set without re-clustering (which drifts as files age or new sessions start). Confidence prevents treating a normal densest pocket as a crash.

## How
- `discover.py` emits: `confidence` (0-1 or enum: high/medium/low), `confidence_reasons[]`, full session list, boot_time, mode, window.
- Scoring heuristics (document in code + tests):
  - high: mode=pre_boot AND cluster_size>=3 AND max|mtime-boot| within window AND densest pocket tight
  - medium: pre_boot with size 1-2, or density with size>=5 near boot
  - low: pure density far from boot or tiny cluster
- Always write plan to `~/.local/state/pfr/last-plan.json` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pfr/`) on every discovery (including dry-run).
- Also write timestamped copy under `~/.local/state/pfr/plans/plan-<iso>.json` (keep last N=20).
- CLI:
  - `--save-plan PATH` optional override path
  - `--plan PATH` open from plan (skip rediscovery)
  - `--last-plan` shorthand for last-plan.json
  - `--print-plan` human summary of confidence + sessions
- Dry-run always saves plan and prints path.
- Open path reads plan, validates schema version, filters missing cwds with warnings.

## Risks
- Schema drift: include `"schema_version": 1`.
- Stale plans opened days later: warn if plan.boot_time != current boot OR plan age > 24h unless `--force-stale-plan`.
- Confidence false positives/negatives: keep reasons list for user override.

## Success criteria
- After `pfr --dry-run`, a plan file exists and `pfr --last-plan --dry-run` shows the same sessions.
- Confidence is high for the known Aug 3 power-loss fixture shape.
- Unit tests cover scoring matrix; e2e covers save/load roundtrip.

title: Rich session identity for pick/list UI
description:
## What
Enrich each discovered session with human-meaningful identity: short title, last user snippet, project name, optional git branch/dirty, message count / size, age relative to boot.

## Why
A list of UUIDs and bare paths is hostile under stress. Swarm tabs share projects; titles prevent opening the wrong fork or stale thread.

## How
- Codex: parse session_meta + scan for first/last user message text (bounded read: first 50 lines + tail 64KB).
- Claude: scan early events for user text; use last-prompt event if present.
- Truncate titles to ~80 chars; sanitize newlines.
- Optional git: if cwd is a git worktree, run `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` (timeout 200ms, best-effort, never fail discovery).
- Display grouping: group table by cwd; within group sort by mtime desc.
- JSON fields: `title`, `preview`, `git_branch`, `git_dirty`, `project_name`, `age_vs_boot_seconds`.
- fzf pick shows: provider | project | title | mtime | short id

## Risks
- Large jsonl tail reads: cap bytes strictly.
- git in huge monorepos slow: timeout + cache per cwd.
- Privacy: titles may contain secrets — plan files should be mode 0600.

## Success criteria
- Dry-run list shows non-empty titles for real frankensim/frankenterm sessions on this machine.
- fzf lines are scannable without UUIDs as primary label.
- Unit tests with fixture jsonl snippets extract expected titles.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: See docs/session-formats.md (distilled from casr): per-message fields include gitBranch, timestamp, version; titles have a first-class priority chain. last_active should come from content timestamps, mtime stays the death signal.

title: Doctor checks + post-boot notify hook
description:
## What
`pfr doctor` health checks + optional macOS Login/LaunchAgent that offers recovery after reboot when confidence is high.

## Why
Power failure recovery fails silently when Automation/Accessibility is missing, Ghostty is absent, or aliases don't load. Post-boot notification makes the tool actually get used when the user is frazzled.

## How
### doctor
Checks (robot JSON + human):
- Ghostty.app present + tip scripting (`new tab` / `input text` smoke via osascript -- optional skip with --no-live)
- System Events process name / binary path detection
- Automation: can talk to Ghostty
- Accessibility: only if keystroke fallback would be needed
- python3, osascript available
- codex sessions dir + claude projects dir exist
- sample discovery runs without error
- plan dir writable
Exit non-zero if any critical check fails; warn for soft issues.

### post-boot
- Document LaunchAgent plist that runs `pfr --auto-boot` ~60s after login
- `--auto-boot`: discover only; if confidence high and cluster_size>=2, show macOS notification (osascript display notification) + write plan; do NOT open tabs unless `--auto-boot-open` (default off for safety)
- `--auto-boot-open` requires explicit config flag in config file (see f6) to prevent surprise API spend

## Risks
- Auto-open could burn tokens/money: default notify-only.
- LaunchAgent spam every login: only notify if confidence high AND plan not already acted on for this boot_time.

## Success criteria
- `pfr doctor` returns structured pass/fail on this Mac.
- Simulated high-confidence plan triggers notification path in dry mode.
- Docs for installing/uninstalling LaunchAgent.

title: Skip already-running + verify opens
description:
## What
**Skip already-running** (implemented — `pfr-skip-running-aen` CLOSED) + **post-open verification** + durable resume report.

## Status of sub-work
- [x] Detect live resumes via `ps` (`resume <uuid>` / `--resume` / `--resume=`); cluster-then-filter; `--force-reopen`
- [ ] Post-open verification polling + `last-report.json` (`pfr-open-verify-3dd`)
- [ ] Tests for verification paths (`pfr-test-verify-opens` — see new bead)
- [ ] Optional window hygiene after verified multi-open (`pfr-hygiene-impl-n7s`)

## Why
Double-resume is costly; silent open failures leave users thinking recovery worked.

## How (remaining: verify)
After each open + settle, poll up to ~8s:
- process table shows `resume <session_id>` OR Ghostty terminal count increased (best-effort)
- Record per-session: `opened | skipped | failed | verified | unverified`
- Write `~/.local/state/pfr/last-report.json`
- Exit 1 if any `failed` (partial resume already does this for open errors — extend with verify)

## Matching rules (already shipped — do not loosen)
UUID must sit immediately after a resume flag; do not match UUIDs merely co-occurring with the word "resume" (editor paths).

## Success criteria
- Re-run after successful recovery: skipped_running > 0, no double tabs without `--force-reopen`
- Forced broken open counts as failed in report
- Unit tests for matching remain green; e2e dry path does not require live agents

title: Unit + e2e test harness with NDJSON logs
description:
## What
Comprehensive unit tests + e2e scripts with detailed NDJSON logging for discovery, clustering, confidence, plans, titles, doctor, verify, config/batch, and Ghostty open invariants.

## Why
Clustering/confidence and open scripts regress easily; every blackout must not be a production test.

## Included test beads (do not drop any)
| Bead | Scope |
|------|--------|
| pfr-test-scaffold-jfl | fixtures, run_tests.sh, logging helper |
| pfr-test-cluster-lhm | densest/pre_boot/dedupe/subagent |
| pfr-plan-tests-n79 | confidence + plan roundtrip |
| pfr-test-e2e-dry-zfi | CLI dry-run + --last-plan |
| pfr-test-titles-2z5 | title/preview extraction |
| pfr-test-verify-7hr | running skip + verify report |
| pfr-test-doctor-6kv | doctor contracts |
| pfr-test-open-scripts-2zx | open script invariants (CI) |
| pfr-test-config-batch-6ga | config + batch pacing |
| pfr-test-audit-gmm | audit log |
| pfr-test-e2e-live-2jq | optional Ghostty live smoke |

## Logging standard
Every e2e/unit group emits NDJSON: `{"ts","step","status","detail",...}` to `tests/logs/`.
On failure: dump last 50 lines to stderr.

## Success
`./scripts/run_tests.sh` exit 0 without Ghostty interaction; live suite opt-in via PFR_LIVE=1.

title: Config file for pfr defaults
description:
## What
User config file for defaults: `~/.config/pfr/config.toml` (or yaml) merged under CLI flags (CLI wins).

## Why
Flags every time after a blackout is friction; auto-boot-open safety switch belongs in config not argv memory.

## Keys (initial)
providers, window_seconds, pre_boot_lookback, driver, settle, delay, max_open, projects_only, auto_boot_open (default false), plan_dir, plan_keep, fake_boot (test only).

## Success
Config changes defaults; CLI still overrides; doctor reports effective config.

title: Install symlink + shell completions
description:
## What
`install.sh` / documented symlink to `~/.local/bin/pfr`, zsh/bash completions for flags.

## Why
Tool only helps if it is on PATH under stress (`pfr` not a long path).

## Success
Fresh shell can run `pfr --help` and complete `--driver`.

title: Audit NDJSON log of recoveries
description:
## What
Append-only audit log of discoveries and opens: `~/.local/state/pfr/audit.ndjson` with ts, action, boot_time, session_ids, results.

## Why
Post-mortem after messy recovery; accretive history for improving confidence heuristics.

## Success
Each dry-run and open appends one or more NDJSON records; `pfr audit --tail 20` prints them.

title: Adaptive shell settle before input text
description:
## What
Instead of fixed settle sleep, optionally poll Ghostty terminal readiness (tty exists, shell pid stable) up to timeout before input text.

## Why
Fixed 0.55s is too short for cold zsh and wastes time when shell is instant — reliability and performance.

## How
AppleScript/osascript: after new tab, poll `pid of terminal` until non-zero and stable for 200ms, or timeout settle_max.

## Success
Slow shell machines succeed with settle_max=3s without always waiting 3s on fast machines.

title: Optional casr metadata enrichment
description:
## What
Optional enrichment: if `casr` is on PATH, merge titles/workspace from `casr list --json` by session_id; never require casr.

## Why
User noted casr is helpful but not required; reuse its metadata for better pick UI without reimplementing all parsers.

## Success
With casr present, titles fill when local parse fails; without casr, behavior unchanged.

title: Faster discovery (parallel + mtime prefilter)
description:
## What
Parallelize codex + claude discovery (threads/process pool); optional mtime prefilter via os.scandir walk that skips old files without opening.

## Why
5169 rollouts is fine today (~100ms) but grows; keep recovery snappy as history accumulates.

## Success
Wall time on this machine not worse than serial; benchmark logged in e2e; no correctness change.

title: Recovery window hygiene (close blank, title tabs)
description:
## What
After successful multi-tab open on a fresh Ghostty launch, close the unused default empty tab; set tab titles to project name via Ghostty scripting if available.

## Why
Clutter and confusion post-recovery; titled tabs match mental model of swarm layout.

## Success
Fresh launch recovery ends with N agent tabs and no blank spare (best-effort).

title: Batched open with pause every N sessions
description:
## What
`--batch-size N` opens N tabs then pauses for Enter (or continues with timeout) to avoid slamming 20+ model sessions at once.

## Why
Cost control and system load after blackout; user can abort mid-batch.

## Success
With batch-size 5 and 12 sessions, exactly two pauses; Ctrl-C leaves report of what opened.

title: Last-user-message preview extraction
description:
## What
Deeper last-user-message extraction for previews (bounded reverse scan of jsonl), shown in --verbose list and plan JSON.

## Why
Complements session-identity titles when first message is a boilerplate system preamble.

## Depends-on conceptually
session-identity feature; can be same module.

## Success
Preview reflects last human intent, not only first line of session.

title: AGENTS.md + README sync for recovery workflows
description:
## What
AGENTS.md for this repo, robot-docs section, update README to match native open path + plan workflow + doctor + tests. Keep human and agent paths aligned.

## Why
Future agents must not rediscover power-failure semantics or reintroduce pgrep -x Ghostty bugs.

## Success
AGENTS.md documents invariants (no delete without permission is global; pfr-specific: never auto-open without config; plan schema).

title: Define plan JSON schema v1 + confidence algorithm
description:
## What
Define plan JSON `schema_version: 1` and pure-function crash **confidence** scoring (`lib/confidence.py` or equivalent). No Ghostty I/O here.

## Why
Auto-boot notify, plan open, and user trust all gate on "is this really a power-failure cluster?" Density-only pockets after a *normal* reboot must never look HIGH.

## Schema v1 (normative fields)
```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "created_at": "<iso8601>",
  "boot_time": <epoch|null>,
  "boot_time_human": "<str|null>",
  "mode": "pre_boot|density|recent|manual_anchor",
  "window_seconds": <float>,
  "pre_boot_lookback": <float>,
  "anchor_mtime": <epoch|null>,
  "confidence": "high|medium|low",
  "confidence_reasons": ["..."],
  "total_candidates_scanned": <int>,
  "skipped_running": <int>,
  "sessions": [
    {
      "provider": "codex|claude",
      "session_id": "<uuid>",
      "cwd": "<path>",
      "mtime": <epoch>,
      "path": "<session file>",
      "resume_cmd": "cod resume …|cc --resume …",
      "title": "<optional>",
      "preview": "<optional>",
      "is_subagent": false,
      "is_running": false
    }
  ]
}
```

## Confidence rubric (lock in unit tests)
1. **HIGH** only if `mode == pre_boot` AND `n >= 3` AND `(boot - anchor) <= window_seconds` AND densest pocket is tight (e.g. span of mtimes within window). Attach reasons like `pre_boot_mode`, `cluster_size=16`, `anchor_within_window_of_boot`.
2. **MEDIUM** if pre_boot with `n in {1,2}` OR density with `n >= 5` AND anchor within pre_boot_lookback of boot.
3. **LOW** otherwise — including pure density far from boot (busy afternoon trap).

**Never mark HIGH for density-only mode**, even if n is large.

## Test injection
- `PFR_FAKE_BOOT` / `--fake-boot EPOCH` for deterministic tests (via discover CLI roots bead).

## Related invariants already learned in-tree (do not regress)
- Cluster **before** filtering already-running sessions (filtering first shifts densest pocket).
- Codex resume id: prefer filename UUID / `session_meta.payload.id` (not parent `session_id`).
- Claude project dirs: non-alphanumeric → `-` encoding; always prefer embedded `cwd` over reverse-decode.

## Success criteria
- Pure unit tests for HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW fixtures without Ghostty
- Golden JSON examples under `tests/fixtures/plans/`

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: REFINEMENT: Pure Python confidence in lib/confidence.py. HIGH only for pre_boot n>=3 tight pocket; never HIGH for density-only. Attach confidence_reasons[]. Use PFR_FAKE_BOOT for tests.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Implement as pure functions; shell already has --force-reopen and process skip. Confidence must integrate with skipped_running field already in discover JSON.

title: Implement plan save/load + CLI --plan/--last-plan/--save-plan
description:
## What
Wire durable recovery plan persistence and CLI flags into `power_failure_resumer.sh` (and thin Python helpers if needed).

## Why
Under stress after a blackout, rediscovery drifts (new sessions, aging mtimes, partial manual resumes). Separating *discover/decide* from *open* is the core reliability upgrade. Empty description was a planning defect — this bead must stay fully self-documenting.

## How
### Paths
- State dir: `~/.local/state/pfr/` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pfr/`), mode `0700`
- `last-plan.json` (atomic write: temp + rename), mode `0600`
- Archive: `plans/plan-<iso8601>.json` (keep last N=20, configurable later via config bead)

### CLI
- Every discovery (including `--dry-run` and `--json`) writes `last-plan.json` unless `--no-save-plan`
- `--save-plan PATH` — write plan to explicit path
- `--plan PATH` — open/list from plan; skip rediscovery
- `--last-plan` — shorthand for state dir last-plan.json
- `--force-stale-plan` — allow plan when `boot_time` ≠ current boot or plan age > 24h
- After dry-run, print:
  ```
  Plan saved: … (confidence=HIGH, N sessions)
  Next: pfr --last-plan -y   OR   pfr --last-plan --pick
  ```

### Schema
Depends on `pfr-plan-schema-l81`. Reject `schema_version != 1` with a clear error. Plan must include confidence + reasons + full session records needed to open without re-scan (provider, session_id, cwd, resume_cmd, mtime, path, titles when available).

### Depends on
- `pfr-plan-schema-l81` (schema + scoring)
- `pfr-discover-cli-roots-2k6` (fixture isolation: `--codex-root`, `--claude-root`, `--fake-boot`, `--state-dir`)

## Risks
- Stale plans after reboot of a different day — warn loudly
- Secrets in titles/previews — file mode 0600; document
- Concurrent Fable edits to shell — re-read before implement

## Success criteria
- `pfr --dry-run` creates last-plan.json; `pfr --last-plan --dry-run` lists identical session_ids
- Stale boot without `--force-stale-plan` refuses open with actionable message
- Unit/e2e coverage via `pfr-plan-tests-n79` and `pfr-test-e2e-dry-zfi`

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: REFINEMENT: After dry-run print plan path + next commands. schema_version must be 1. Atomic write temp+rename. state dir 0700 plan files 0600. --force-stale-plan for boot mismatch.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: DISCOVER-CLI-ROOTS is CLOSED (shipped). Plan CLI implementation should use --codex-root/--claude-root/--fake-boot/--state-dir already on the tree; re-read shell before editing (Fable concurrent).

title: Unit tests for confidence + plan roundtrip
description:
## What
Unit tests for confidence scoring + plan save/load roundtrip e2e with NDJSON logging.

## Why
Locks the crash-signature quality so density fallback cannot silently look HIGH.

## Coverage
### Unit
- HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW fixtures with fake boot + synthetic session mtimes
- Never HIGH when mode=density
- pre_boot n=16 tight pocket → HIGH
- pre_boot n=1 → MEDIUM
- Schema reject version≠1

### E2E (script)
- dry-run with fixture roots → last-plan.json exists mode 0600
- --last-plan --dry-run session_id set equality
- stale boot without --force-stale-plan fails open path

## Logging
`tests/logs/plan-tests-<ts>.ndjson` — one event per case with expected vs actual confidence.

## Depends on
plan-schema, plan-cli, test-scaffold

## Success
Included in `./scripts/run_tests.sh`; exit 0 offline.

title: Extract titles/previews from codex+claude transcripts
description:
## What
Bounded parse of Codex + Claude session files for human **title** and **preview** fields used by list/fzf/plan JSON.

## Why
UUID lists are unusable under stress; swarm tabs share project cwds.

## How (provider-accurate — informed by casr study, do not depend on casr)
### Codex
- `session_meta.payload` for cwd / id
- First meaningful user text from `response_item` / `event_msg` user_message (bounded: first 50 lines + optional tail 64KB later)
- Title fallback: project basename from cwd

### Claude Code
- Prefer embedded `cwd` always
- Title priority (casr-aligned): **`custom-title` / customTitle** (user `/rename`) > **`ai-title` / aiTitle** > **`summary`** > first user message text
- `message.content` may be string OR array of content blocks — flatten text blocks only
- Project dir keys replace *every* non-alphanumeric with `-` (not just `/`); never reverse-decode for truth

### Bounds
- Cap bytes/lines strictly; never throw on parse errors; return empty title rather than crash discovery

## Success criteria
- Real frankensim/frankenterm/claude sessions on this Mac yield non-empty titles in `--json` when content exists
- Unit tests with fixtures for custom-title vs ai-title priority and content-block flattening
- Plan files remain mode 0600 once plan CLI lands (titles may contain sensitive prompt text)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: casr (~/projects/cross_agent_session_resumer) has this solved: Claude title priority is custom-title (user /rename) > ai-title > summary > first user text; codex has agent_nickname + first user msg. Copy the ideas, not the dependency. See docs/session-formats.md.

title: Group list/fzf by project; show git branch best-effort
description:
## What
Human table + fzf multi-select UX grouped by project with titles and best-effort git branch.

## Why
Swarm tabs share cwds; UUID-primary lists cause wrong resumes under stress.

## How
- Group sessions by cwd; within group sort mtime desc
- Display columns: #, provider, time, project/title, short cwd
- fzf: tab-delimited; fields num, provider, mtime, title|project, resume_cmd — must tolerate spaces in paths (already)
- Git: per unique cwd, `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` + dirty check with 200ms timeout; cache; never fail discovery
- Show age vs boot when boot known

## Depends on
extract-titles

## Tests
Covered indirectly by e2e dry snapshot of list output; title tests ensure data present.

## Success
Dry-run groups frankensim sessions; fzf shows titles not raw UUIDs as primary label.

title: Implement pfr doctor (JSON + human)
description:
## What
Implement `pfr doctor` (or `./power_failure_resumer.sh --doctor`) with human + `--json` output.

## Why
Silent Automation/Ghostty/path failures are the #1 real-world "recovery does nothing" mode.

## Checks (each: name, status pass|warn|fail, detail)
### Critical (fail → exit ≠ 0)
- python3 available
- osascript available
- discover.py present and importable
- open_sessions*.applescript present
- state dir creatable/writable
- codex sessions dir exists (or warn if provider disabled)
- claude projects dir exists (or warn)

### Important (fail or warn)
- Ghostty.app exists at /Applications/Ghostty.app (or custom path)
- Can AppleScript `tell application "Ghostty" to get name` (Automation)
- Tip scripting: `new surface configuration` / new tab smoke optional with `--doctor-live`

### Soft (warn only)
- Accessibility (only if keystroke fallback would be needed)
- `cod`/`cc` resolvable in login zsh (`zsh -lic 'type cod; type cc'`)

## Output
- Human: checkmarks + summary
- JSON: `{ "ok": bool, "checks": [ ... ] }`

## Success
Doctor exits 0 on healthy Mac; simulated missing Ghostty → fail; tests in `pfr-test-doctor-6kv`.

comments.author: Codex
comments.text:
Fresh-eyes review while this bead is active:
1. ShellCheck SC2015 on lines 374-384: replace A && add_ok || add_warn with explicit if/else; add_ok failure can wrongly enter warn branch.
2. State-dir probe creates then rm -f deletes .doctor-probe, violating parent AGENTS.md no-delete invariant. Prefer a non-mutating nearest-existing-parent writable/executable check.
3. JSON TSV pipeline breaks if a check detail contains tabs/newlines; use NUL-delimited records or direct JSON construction.
4. agent_mail detail says will open a tab, but no open behavior exists; phrase as optional availability.
5. Bead asks for cod/cc login-shell checks; current implementation checks fzf/am instead.

comments.author: Codex
comments.text: Also: the concurrent qcmd change in open_one_ghostty is behavior-breaking. printf %q turns `cod resume UUID` into `cod\ resume\ UUID`; passing that as the shell -c program attempts one command name containing spaces. The resume command is now reconstructed from provider+validated UUID at the TSV boundary, so keep `-ic "$resume_cmd"` (or use a safe literal dispatch), not `%q` of the whole command.

title: Post-boot notify mode + LaunchAgent docs
description:
## What
`--auto-boot` discovers, scores, writes plan, and **notifies** when confidence is HIGH. Opens tabs only if config `auto_boot_open=true` (default **false**).

## Why
Users under stress may not remember to run pfr; surprise multi-open burns money and is unsafe.

## How
- Run ~60s after login via LaunchAgent (documented install/uninstall plist)
- If confidence high AND cluster_size ≥ 2 AND not already acted for this boot_time → `osascript` display notification
- Body: "N sessions ready — run: pfr --last-plan"
- Dedup: if last-report or audit shows acted for same boot_time, skip notify
- `--auto-boot-open` requires config file key true; CLI alone must not enable

## Depends on
plan-schema, plan-cli, config-load

## Success
Notify path works in dry simulation; LaunchAgent docs complete; no open by default; tests assert auto_boot_open default false.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: REFINEMENT SAFETY: auto_boot_open default false requires config true. Notify-only by default. Dedupe notifications per boot_time if already acted.

title: Detect already-running sessions by cmdline UUID
description:
## What
pgrep/ps scan for exact session UUID in agent process args; mark skip.

## Why
Double resume is costly and dangerous.

## Success

title: Post-open verification + last-report.json
description:
## What
After each Ghostty open, verify the resume likely took; write `last-report.json`; exit non-zero on hard failures.

## Why
osascript can return 0 while input never landed; users need an honest partial-resume report.

## How
### Per session after open_one
Poll up to `--verify-timeout` (default 8s, 0.5s interval):
1. Prefer process match: live cmdline with `resume <session_id>` (reuse tight matcher from skip-running)
2. Else best-effort: Ghostty terminal count increased (AppleScript) — mark `unverified` not `verified` if only this signal
3. If open_one failed → `failed`
4. If skipped as already running → `skipped`

### Report path
`~/.local/state/pfr/last-report.json` (or `--state-dir`):
```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "created_at": "...",
  "driver": "ui|api",
  "results": [{"session_id","provider","status","detail"}],
  "counts": {"opened","verified","unverified","skipped","failed"}
}
```

### Exit codes
- 0: no `failed`
- 1: any `failed` OR (optional strict) any `unverified` with `--verify-strict`

## Coordination with open scripts
Do not reintroduce: default-tab reuse, double Cmd+T after partial native success, loose UUID matching.

## Depends on
- `pfr-skip-running-aen` (CLOSED — matcher exists)
- Tests: `pfr-test-verify-7hr`

## Success
Report written on every open run; dry-run does not require Ghostty; unit tests cover status aggregation.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: SKIP-RUNNING is CLOSED with tight resume-flag matching + cluster-then-filter. This bead is pure post-open verification + last-report.json.

title: Fixture-based discover clustering unit tests
description:
## What
Fixture-based unit tests for densest_cluster, pre_boot isolation, dedupe, subagent filter, and **cluster-then-filter-running** order.

## Why
Core product logic; power-loss signature and already-running interaction must stay correct.

## Coverage (mandatory cases)
1. Densest window prefers higher count; ties prefer newer window
2. pre_boot set with early outlier 13min before boot + crash pocket at boot → densest drops outlier
3. Dedupe keeps newest mtime per (provider, session_id)
4. Subagent thread_source/source.subagent excluded by default
5. **Regression:** marking majority of crash cluster as running must NOT change which pocket densest_cluster selects (filter only after cluster)
6. Filename UUID preferred for codex resume id when meta missing

## Logging
NDJSON per case: name, status, detail (expected ids vs actual).

## Depends on
test-scaffold; uses discover.py functions directly

## Success
All cases pass in run_tests.sh without live home session dirs (fixtures only).

title: Merge casr list metadata when available
description:
## What

## Why
User noted casr is helpful for structure knowledge; optional enrichment can fill titles when local parse is thin without reimplementing full converters.

## How
- Detect casr via `command -v casr`
- `casr list --json --limit N` best-effort; timeout 5s
- Join on session_id; only fill empty title/workspace fields (local parse wins if present)
- Feature flag: config `casr_enrich = true` default false OR `--casr-enrich`

## Non-goals
- Do not shell out to casr for clustering or resume
- Do not vendor casr

## Depends on
extract-titles (local path must work first)

## Success
Without casr: identical behavior; with casr + flag: richer titles when local empty; unit test with mocked casr JSON fixture.
